A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TOC/TICL study and include appendices A–G. Text, equations, tables and embedded figures support reliable comparison. Figure 18 in v2 is partly outside the page boundary, but its embedded content is recoverable.

before.justification: v1 reports original timestamp-estimation, retrieval, video-classification and image-editing experiments, including quantitative evaluations and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds VQA comparisons, season/hour prediction, a contrastive-loss comparison and dataset brightness analysis.

M1.justification: The default TICL architecture, InfoNCE objective and inference pipelines remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 adds joint season/hour supervision, while C.3 introduces an experimental SegSort-style variant using hour-specific clustering and nearest-neighbour inference; InfoNCE remains the default.

E1.justification: The datasets and principal downstream tasks are retained. Appendix B.4 adds joint season-and-hour prediction on TOC beyond v1's hour/month tasks; no new dataset or domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds BLIP-VQA-base and GPT-4o-mini as direct VQA comparators, and new Table 8 evaluates a SegSort-style alternative. Existing timestamp, retrieval, video and editing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New comparisons introduce single-round VQA prompting for HH:MM predictions and a SegSort configuration with 25 subclusters per hour, 10 k-means iterations per refresh and concentration 10. Existing splits, metrics, training budgets and downstream evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 supplements the existing analyses with a before/after-cleaning brightness check (Figure 13), season-supervision and embedding analysis (B.4), and an alternative contrastive-objective comparison (C.3). The previous backbone, encoding, class-granularity and video-consistency analyses remain.

E5.justification: New Figure 13 reports hourly mean brightness with standard-deviation error bars before and after cleaning. This adds dataset-dispersion reporting, not repeated-run model uncertainty. Existing user-study standard deviations remain unchanged; no new seed counts, run counts or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing scores are retained, with additional VQA, season/hour and SegSort results. For example, GPT-4o-mini achieves 15.35% TOC top-1 accuracy and 161.39-minute MAE (Table 2); joint season/hour TICL reports 20.14% hour accuracy and 61.52% season accuracy (Table 7). Brightness statistics and retrieval-error means are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The InfoNCE formula, regression and cyclic-encoding reasoning, class-partitioning analysis and image-editing optimization formulas are retained. The additions introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: TOC provides reliable timestamps, TICL improves time estimation, and its representations support retrieval, video classification and image editing.

C2.justification: B.4 newly links season supervision to possible timestamp calibration, while C.3 hypothesizes that object-driven clustering explains the SegSort variant's limitations. A.1 interprets the added brightness check as supporting cleaning quality. Existing ambiguity and nighttime-data limitations remain.

D1.justification: B.2 supplies the exact VQA prompt, and C.3 documents clustering hyperparameters and the frozen training-embedding gallery. The project-page address also changes. These are additional implementation and access details; the PDFs do not establish newly available downloadable resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for BLIP, the GPT-4o system card and SegSort. Section 3 more explicitly positions semantic time embeddings as the novelty, and A.1 tabulates differences from existing datasets. The principal related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 revises the method explanation, renames Section 5.3 to Detailed component analysis, adds subsection C.3 and moves references after the appendices. Author information and publication headers change, while the main narrative and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds dataset-comparison and contrastive-loss tables, dataset-issue and brightness figures, and a season-embedding plot. Tables 2 and 7 expand, and Figure 6 gains mean-error legends. Existing displays are mostly retained or repositioned; new Figure 18 is clipped below page 18.

improvement.justification: The added VQA comparisons, contrastive-loss ablation and brightness sanity check modestly strengthen empirical support for the existing study. Explicit settings help readers assess the additions. Figure 18's clipping and limited season-label construction details reduce the usefulness of the new season analysis, but do not outweigh the added evidence.
